column2: On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both), who said: I was behind the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) one day, and he said: “O young man, I will teach you some words: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you. Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. When you ask, ask Allah;

and when you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the nation were to gather together to benefit you with something, they would not benefit you except with something Allah has already written for you; and if they were to gather together to harm you with something, they would not harm you except with something Allah has already written against you.
The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.”
Reported by al-Tirmidhī, who said: A ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.

In a narration other than al-Tirmidhī's: “Be mindful of Allah and you will find Him in front of you. Get to know Allah in times of ease and He will know you in times of hardship. Know that what has missed you was not going to befall you,
and what has befallen you was not going to miss you. Know that victory comes with patience, relief comes with distress, and with hardship comes ease.”
“Behind the Prophet ﷺ”: riding behind him on his mount.

Yā ghulām (“O young man”): with ḍammah on the mīm, because it is an indefinite noun specifically addressed. A ghulām is a boy from weaning until nine years of age; his age at that time was about ten years.
“I will teach you some words (kalimāt)”: by which Allah will benefit you; the tanwīn here expresses magnification.
“Be mindful of Allah”: by holding constantly to fear of Him and avoiding what He has forbidden;
“and He will protect you”: in yourself and your family, your worldly life and your religion, especially at death.
“Be mindful of Allah”: as above.
Tujāhaka (“before you”): with ḍammah on the tāʾ; in front of you, as in the narration that follows.
“When you ask”: when you want to ask,
“ask Allah”: to give you what you seek, and do not ask anyone else, for he has no power to benefit or harm himself, let alone anyone else.
Istaʿanta (“you seek help”): you seek assistance in any matter of this world or the Hereafter,
“seek help from Allah”: because He has power over all things, while everyone else is incapable even of securing what is good for himself and warding off what harms him.
Al-ummah (“the nation”): what is meant here is all created beings.
“The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried”: an expression meaning that all decrees were written long ago and have long been completed.
Taʿarraf (“get to know”): with the rāʾ doubled.
“Allah in times of ease”: by keeping constantly to obedience to Him and spending in the ways that bring one near [to Him].
“And He will know you in times of hardship”: by relieving it for you and making for you, from every difficulty, relief, and from every worry, a way out.
“Know that what has missed you”: of the decrees, and did not reach you,
“was not going to befall you”: because it was decreed for someone else.
“And what has befallen you”: of them,
“was not going to miss you”: because it was decreed for you.
Wa-ʿlam (“know”): [a word of] alerting.
“That victory”: from Allah for the servant over all the enemies of his religion and his worldly life, wherever they may be,
“comes with patience”: in obeying Allah, in refraining from disobeying Him, and in calamities.
Al-faraj (“relief”): coming out of grief.
Al-karb (“distress”): grief that overwhelms the soul.
The printed text reads جوه القرب, evidently for وجوه القرب (“the ways that bring one near”).
It is permissible to have someone ride behind one on a mount, if it can bear it.
A teacher may tell the learner that he wants to teach him before doing so, so that his eagerness for what he will learn increases and he gives it his full attention.
The command to guard and observe the rights of Allah the Exalted.
The recompense may be of the same kind as the deed.
The command to rely on Allah and put one's trust in Him rather than anyone else, since He is the One who benefits and harms. Allah the Exalted said:

“If Allah touches you with harm, none can remove it but Him; and if He intends good for you, none can repel His bounty” [Yūnus 10:107]. To the extent that a person leans on other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in his requests,

his heart or his hopes, he has turned away from his Lord to one who can neither harm nor benefit him—especially when what he asks for is something that does not customarily come about at the hands of created beings, such as guidance,
the cure of illness, well-being from the trials of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and the like, which none but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has power over.
The helplessness of all created beings and their need of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Drawing attention to the fact that this abode is exposed to calamities, so one should be patient with them.
Contentment with the decision and decree.
